title: Dispatch: Enforce strictly-prospective ordinary lifecycle admission (PR #524 review 4, head f886c24)
description:
External review #5118495204 (2026-09-04) of PR #524 head f886c24, semantic-system profile: CHANGES REQUIRED, ONE blocking finding. Supervisor independently REPRODUCED it at f886c24 (see below). Everything else on the PR — the prior external blockers and all six local self-review rounds — was re-checked by the reviewer and stands.

WORKTREE / BRANCH
.worktrees/eshyra-jhpt.rev10 on branch eshyra-jhpt.rev10, cut from eshyra-jhpt at f886c24. npm ci already run.

# =============================================================
FINDING (BLOCKING) — ordinary lifecycle mutations at the latest persisted position rewrite that turn's canonical history.

Invariant (eshyra-jhpt.1/.2/.5/.8, ADR 0020 state integrity): ordinary campaign rules and lifecycle changes are PROSPECTIVE; retroactivity is reserved for the explicit disputed-turn mode bounded to the current or immediately-preceding turn. assertCurrentPosition defines currentPosition as the latest PERSISTED campaign_turn_position row. That row is created inside the turn savepoint and survives only when the turn commits, so "currentPosition" at a management call is an ALREADY-ADJUDICATED turn. The live boundary rejects `< currentPosition` but accepts `== currentPosition` in all three ordinary mutations:

- create: checkTemporalMode (campaignRules.ts) rejects prospective effectivePosition only when `< currentPosition`. A rule effective at P10 with current P10 is accepted and activeRows(P10) immediately includes it.
- revoke: revokeCampaignRule rejects only `revokedPosition < currentPosition`; combined with assertPersistedPosition (revokedPosition must be a persisted row) the ONLY admissible non-future revocation is P10 itself, and activeRows keeps a revoked rule only while revoked_position > cutoff, so P10 flips to inactive. There is currently NO genuinely prospective revocation path for an active rule at all.
- supersede: the prospective successor is rejected only when `effectivePosition < currentPosition`; successor at P10 rewrites the rule set P10 used.

SUPERVISOR REPRODUCTION at f886c24 (bareDb, rule 'early' effective ordinal 1 created at current ordinal 0, then ten resolveCampaignPosition turns so persisted current = P10; activeRows queried at P10 after each ordinary mutation with currentPosition = P10):
  create before      ["early"]
  create after       ["early","late"]        <- 'late' effective P10
  revoke after       ["late"]                <- 'early' revoked at P10
  supersede after    ["late2"]               <- 'late' superseded by 'late2' effective P10
All three succeeded and each changed P10's active set.

# =============================================================
REQUIRED SEMANTICS (supervisor decision — implement exactly this; if you find it incoherent with replay, say so in your notes rather than inventing an alternative)

Ordinary (prospective-mode) admission is STRICTLY AFTER the persisted current position:
1. create: prospective effectivePosition.ordinal must be > currentPosition.ordinal. `==` is rejected with a distinctive message, e.g. 'prospective campaign rule cannot take effect at or before the current position' (update the existing '< current' message/guard in checkTemporalMode; keep a single guard). The existing future canonicalization (canonicalizeFutureEffectivePosition -> __future__ anchor) then applies to every admitted prospective rule, so there is no fabricated-anchor path left for prospective creation. Bootstrap (no persisted row, current ordinal 0) is unchanged: effective ordinal >= 1.
2. supersede: same rule for a prospective successor — effective ordinal must be > current ordinal, canonicalized to the __future__ anchor. The prior's interval therefore ends strictly after the current turn: prior still active at P10, successor active from P11. Disputed-turn successors keep today's bounded current/immediately-previous checks unchanged.
3. revoke: revokedPosition.ordinal must be > currentPosition.ordinal (distinctive message, e.g. "campaign rule 'x' cannot be revoked at or before the current position"). Since such a position cannot be persisted yet, DROP assertPersistedPosition for revokedPosition and instead canonicalize it to the __future__ anchor exactly as create does for effective positions (add a shared helper rather than duplicating). Because __future__ sorts BEFORE a real anchor at the same ordinal, a rule revoked at future(11) is active at real P10 and inactive at real P11 — verify this against compareCampaignPositions and activeRows and assert it in tests. Ordinary between-turn revocation is then: revokedPosition = { ordinal: current+1 } (any session/turn ids; they are replaced by the anchor).
4. Future-rule cancellation (round-5 fix): a rule scheduled at ordinal E > current may still be cancelled; it now happens with revokedPosition.ordinal > current (typically current+1), which may be < E. Decide and DOCUMENT one canonical representation — either store the given future revokedPosition (activeRows already yields "never active" because effective > cutoff for every cutoff < E and revoked <= cutoff for every cutoff >= revoked) or canonicalize revokedPosition up to the effective position. Either way the round-5 guarantee holds: the rule is never active at any position, and the current position's active set is unchanged by the cancellation. Retire the now-unreachable canCancelBeforeEffective / 'cannot be revoked before its effective position' branch only if it is genuinely unreachable under the new admission; if you keep a guard, its test must be able to fail.
5. Disputed-turn mode is UNCHANGED: creation/supersession at the current or immediately-preceding turn (including the cross-session adjacent case) remains accepted, with persisted-anchor validation as today.
6. All rejected mutations remain atomic: no row, chain, or historical active-at-position change on rejection (already inside withTransaction — assert it).

Do NOT change: the position encoding, migrations, eshyra-jhpt.2.5, eshyra-umyb, eshyra-l30k, the ambiguity-overlap algebra (re-check that intervalsOverlap/existingIntervalEnd still agree with the new successor/revocation positions — the successor now starts at a __future__ anchor), or any round 1-6 property (real stored prior status validated; returned rule deep-equals persisted; single active-row scan; transactional mutations).

# =============================================================
PERMANENT REGRESSION EVIDENCE (reviewer's list — cover the generalized boundary, each must FAIL against f886c24)
E1. After committed P10: ordinary create effective at P10 (current P10) is rejected with the guard message; activeRows(P10) identical before/after. Create at ordinal 11 succeeds, is stored with the __future__ anchor, is inactive at P10 and active at real P11 once turn 11 is persisted.
E2. Revoking an active rule after committed P10 cannot make it inactive at P10: revocation at P10 rejected; revocation at ordinal 11 succeeds; rule active at P10, inactive at real P11.
E3. Ordinary supersession at P10 rejected; successor at 11 succeeds; P10 history unchanged (prior active, successor absent); at P11 prior superseded, successor active.
E4. Disputed-turn creation AND supersession at the current and immediately-previous turn still accepted, including cross-session adjacency.
E5. Future-rule cancellation at current+1: rule never active at current, at E, or after; current active set unchanged.
E6. Rejected mutations leave rows/chains/active-at-position results unchanged (assert via listCampaignRules + activeRows before/after).
Every negative assertion asserts the distinctive guard message. Update existing tests that legitimately mutated at the current position (e.g. 'applies supersession and revocation prospectively', the ambiguity-overlap and transaction tests, contextAssembler tests) to the new admission rather than weakening them; report which tests changed and why. NEGATIVE PROOF: run the new/changed tests against f886c24 before fixing and report observed failed/passed counts with the asserted messages.

VERIFICATION
npm run verify:worktree BEFORE committing. Report pass/skip counts and confirm worktree-local resolution.
